newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 97 industrial output seen up 8.5 pct-report.
newsitem.headline: Polish 97 industrial output seen up 8.5 pct-report.

text.p: Poland's industrial output is likely to grow by 8.5 percent in 1997, against 8.8 percent last year, Poland's Government Centre for Strategic Studies (CSS) said in a report on Wednesday.
CSS said the construction output should rise by 13 percent this year, up from 1996 growth of 6.4 percent.

It said industrial and construction firms expected a further improvement of business climate in the next few months. They saw demand and employment growth, falls in stocks and an improvement in their financial standing.
It said the processing industry's output, which currently amounted to 80 percent of the overal industrial output, was likely to keep growing at a fast pace, while mining output would fall.
It said the construction industry was benefitting from a mild winter, with output in the January-April period 27.8 percent higher than in the same period last year.
CSS said, however, the rapid growth figures were also partly a result of last year's low base for comparison.
It said the number of dwellings likely to be completed in 1997 would rise for the first time since 1991, to 65,000 up from last year's 59,000.
In the January-April period 17,100 dwellings were completed, 9.5 percent more than in the same period last year.
The report said investment demand in Poland was likely to grow by about 18 percent, down from last year's growth of 22.1 percent.
